399: A double-membrane vesicle that sequesters a portion of cytoplasm or an organelle to deliver it to the lysosome. It arises from a phagophore formed in contact with the ER (ULK1 and VPS34–Beclin 1 complexes), grows thanks to the ATG5–ATG12–ATG16L1 system and lipid-linked LC3, then fuses with a lysosome. Receptors such as p62 target ubiquitinated cargo to it.
400: In the erythroblast, mitophagy (NIX receptor) removes all mitochondria at the end of maturation.
401: In the fasting hepatocyte, autophagy releases amino acids, glycogen and lipids (lipophagy).
402: In the neuron, many autophagosomes form at the tip of the axon and travel back to the soma, where the lysosomes are.
404: A membraneless condensate formed by phase separation. It gathers untranslated mRNAs and the enzymes that degrade them: the decapping complex DCP1–DCP2 and its activators (DDX6, LSM1–7, EDC4), the 5′→3′ exonuclease XRN1, and the Argonaute and GW182 proteins of the microRNA pathway. mRNAs are stored or destroyed there.
